intro: In lesson 67, you learnt to make questions with did: Who did you call? But when the question word (who, what, which…) is the SUBJECT of the verb, we do not use do, does or did: Who called? This small difference changes the meaning of the question completely, and it is a classic difficulty for learners.
objectifs: Tell the difference between a subject question (Who called you?) and an object question (Who did you call?).
Make subject questions with no auxiliary and the normal verb form (Who lives here? What happened?).
Use who, what, which and how many as subjects.
Answer subject questions correctly (Anna did. / My brother does.).

texte: Compare: Anna called Marc. If you don't know the person who called (the subject), you ask: Who called Marc? → Anna. If you don't know the person who received the call (the object), you ask: Who did Anna call? → Marc.
In a subject question, who simply takes the place of the subject: the word order is the same as in a statement. No change of order, no do / does / did.
Tip: ask yourself if the answer is the person who DOES the action (subject → no auxiliary) or the person the action happens TO (object → do / does / did).

lignes: What ate my sandwich? → The dog.
What did the dog eat? → My sandwich.

exemples: Who did you call last night?

texte: In the present, the verb takes the -s of he / she / it, because who and what work like “he / she / it”: Who lives here? Who wants coffee? What makes you happy?
In the past, use the past simple form directly: Who broke the window? What happened? Who won the match?
With be and modal verbs, it's the same idea: Who is at the door? Who was absent? Who can help me? Who will come?

sections.titre: Which, whose, how many as subjects
texte: Question words followed by a noun can also be subjects: Which team won? Whose phone is ringing? How many people came?
Compare: How many people came? (subject: people came) / How many people did you invite? (object: you invited people).
What + noun works in the same way: What music relaxes you? / What music do you listen to?
exemples: Which bus goes to the airport?
How many students passed the exam?

texte: The short answer uses the subject + the auxiliary for the tense: Who called? — Anna did. Who lives here? — My aunt does. Who is ready? — I am.
In speech, people often answer with just the name or an object pronoun: Who wants tea? — Me! (very common), or more carefully: I do.
Be careful: even if the answer is plural, the question stays singular: Who lives in that house? — The Mbarga family. / My cousins do.
exemples: Who made this cake? — My sister did.
Who speaks Spanish here? — Carlos does.

texte: Trap 1: adding did from habit. “Who did call you?” is not the normal question (a stressed did is only possible for strong emphasis). The normal form is Who called you?
Trap 2: forgetting the -s in the present. Who knows the answer? (not “Who know”).
Trap 3: “what happen” without an ending. In the past: What happened? In the present, for something general: What happens when…?

formule: Subject question: Who / What / Which + noun / How many + noun + verb (no auxiliary) · Who called? · Object question: Who + did + subject + base form? · Who did you call?
prononciation: In a subject question, the stress often falls on the verb and the main information: Who CALLED? What HAPPENED?
who /huː/: breathe out the h clearly; don't say “oo”.
Who's = Who is or Who has: Who's there? /huːz/.
In the short answer, the auxiliary is stressed: ANna DID. My SIster DOES.
erreurs: Who is the subject: no did.
What is the subject: no did.
Who + he / she / it form of the verb.
If who is the object, you need did.
How many people is the subject.
Always -s, even if the answer is plural.
Who broke the vase? — My brother broke.

dialogue.contexte: In a shared flat in Brussels, Yasmine comes home from work and finds the kitchen in a mess.
lignes: What happened here? Who used all the plates?
Not me! Théo did. He cooked for his friends.
About ten. And who did he invite? Half of his football team!
Object question: who did he invite.
Great… And who's going to wash all this?
Subject question with be going to.
Hmm. Who ate my yoghurt? It was in the fridge.
I don't know… Which yoghurt? The one with strawberries?
Yes! Lucas… what did you eat for breakfast?
Object question: what did you eat.

mots: make something go into pieces or stop working
be the best in a game or competition
ask someone to come to a party, a meal…
make a sound (a phone, a bell)
say that you will certainly do something
The milk is in the fridge.
a cold box in the kitchen for food
Put the plates on the table.

exercices.consigne: Read the sentence, then ask two questions with who: one about the subject and one about the object.
items: Who helped Awa? (Paul) / Who did Paul help? (Awa)
Who phoned the doctor? / Who did your mother phone?
Who loves Karim? / Who does Sara love?
Who saw Léo? / Who did the teacher see?

exercices.consigne: Ask the subject question for the part in CAPITALS.
items: Who won the match? / Which team won the match?
TWENTY PEOPLE came to the meeting.
How many people came to the meeting?
You want to know the writer of this book. (Who wrote / Who did write) this book?
You want to know the thing your friend bought. (What bought you / What did you buy)?
You heard a noise. Something fell. (What fell / What did fall)?
Marc met someone. You want to know the person. (Who met Marc / Who did Marc meet)?

exercices.consigne: Each sentence has one mistake. Correct it.
items: Who you saw at the market?
Who did you see at the market?
How many students did pass the test?
How many students passed the test?

exercices.consigne: Write one question for each situation.
items: Someone told your friend a secret. You want to know the person.
You see an accident in the street. You ask a person near you.
Your friend saw someone yesterday. You want to know the person.
You are making tea. You want to know the people who want some.

exercices.consigne: Imagine a small mystery at work or at home (something disappeared or got broken). Write four subject questions (Who…? What…? How many…? Whose…?) and two object questions with did.
items: Who opened the window? What happened to the plant? How many people came in this morning? Whose bag is this? What did the cleaner see? Who did the manager call?

a_retenir: Subject question: Who / What + verb, no do / does / did (Who called? What happened?).
Object question: Who / What + did + subject + base form (Who did you call?).
In the present: Who lives…? (singular verb with -s).
Which / Whose / How many + noun can be subjects: How many people came?
Short answers: Anna did. / My aunt does. / I am.
